params: {group?: name (only that colour group's swatches)} → {swatches: [{name, kind: "none"|"color"|"gradient"|"pattern", group, global, spot, color?, hex?, tintOf?: base swatch of a tint swatch, tint?: its %, gradient?, pattern?}] (the built-in [Registration] after None: it prints on every plate and can't be edited, moved or deleted), groups: [{name, swatches: [names]}]}

label: Move Swatch
params: {name? | names?: [swatch names, in order; or colour group names to reorder the groups], to?: index in the destination (they go before the swatch or group now there; default: the end), group?: destination colour group (default: the ungrouped swatches; groups hold solid colours only)} reorder swatches or move them into or out of colour groups, as one undo step → {moved}

label: Add Used Colors
params: {selection?: false (only the selected art's colours; default: all the art's), global?: false (the new swatches are global and the matching unlinked colours in that art link to them)} add a swatch for each colour used (fills, strokes, text, gradient stops, mesh points) that no solid swatch has yet, as one undo step → {added: [names], linked}

label: Select All Unused
params: {} → {names: [the swatches nothing uses, in panel order]}: a colour is used when a paint links to it or an unlinked paint, gradient stop or mesh point has its colour; a gradient when a gradient links to it or has its stops; a pattern when it fills or strokes anything (art, symbols, pattern tiles and graphic styles count). None is never listed

label: Merge Swatches
params: {names: [two or more solid-colour swatches], name?: the merged swatch's name (one swatch kept)} keep the first (its name and colour) and delete the others; paints linked to them take its colour and link to it (or unlink when it isn't global), as one undo step → {name, merged: [deleted names], relinked}

label: Ungroup Color Group
params: {name: colour group} move its swatches to the end of the ungrouped swatches and remove the group, as one undo step → {swatches: [names]}

label: Sort by Kind
params: {} order the swatches of each list by kind (None first, then process colours, spot colours, gradients, patterns; colour groups stay after them), keeping their order within a kind, as one undo step

label: Spot Colors
params: {useLab?: bool (omitted: unchanged)} the document's Spot Colors options: spot colours defined in Lab show, print and export from their Lab values (true, the default: PDF Separation spaces get a Lab alternate) or from their working-CMYK equivalents (false: a DeviceCMYK alternate, matching older files). Art, gradient stops and tint swatches linked to Lab spot swatches take the chosen colour at their tint, as one undo step → {useLab, relinked: paints changed}

label: Edit Color Group
params: {group: colour group, colors: [colour] (hex, key, {c,m,y,k} or {l,a,b}; the group's swatches take them in order, extra colours become new swatches, swatches past the end are removed; built-in swatches can't change; a color the swatch already has keeps its model), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), rename?: new group name} rewrite a colour group as one undo step; art linked to its global swatches takes their new colours (and keeps its colour, unlinked, when its swatch goes) → {name, swatches: [names], relinked}

label: Gradient
params: {stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), kind?: linear|radial|freeform (freeform places points on each object, coloured along the stops), mode?: points|lines (freeform: how the Gradient tool adds points), method?: classic|perceptual (how the colours between the stops mix: in display RGB, or perceptually (OKLab) so the steps look even, which SVG and PDF exports draw as an image, except that PDF writes one with spot color stops in its inks when every other stop is paper white, CMYK or gray; freeform gradients mix their own way), stops?: [{offset 0..1, color? (needed without swatch), opacity? 0..1 (or 0..100), midpoint? 0.13..0.87, swatch?: colour swatch name (a global or spot colour or tint swatch links the stop, so swatch edits recolour it and a spot stop prints on its plate; a process colour just gives its colour), tint?: 0..100 (% of the linked swatch; default 100, or a tint swatch's own)}] (at least 2; a freeform gradient's points are recoloured along them), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill; a stop color the gradient already has keeps its model), angle?: deg, aspect?: %, reverse?: bool, dither?: bool (fills only: a linear or radial gradient fill is drawn with fine noise that hides banding, and as pixels in SVG and PDF exports), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), ids?|id?, strokeMode?: within|along|across (strokes only: the gradient lies on the page and shows through the stroke, runs from the start of each subpath to its end, or runs from the stroke's left edge to its right all along it; with nothing selected, for the next object drawn; type characters' own strokes always paint within), target?: "object"|"contents"} edit the gradient in place (keeps its placement); solid/none paints become the default gradient

label: Gradient Vector
params: {start?: [x,y], end?: [x,y] (document coordinates; both or neither: omitted, the vector stays), aspect?: % (radial: the extent ellipse's height / width; default: kept), focal?: [x,y] (document coordinates) | null (radial: the focal point, where the first stop sits, pulled inside the extent ellipse; null centres it; default: it keeps its place in the ellipse), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (alias: index; omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents", index?: appearance item index (as item)} set the gradient vector, aspect ratio and focal point (solid paints become the default gradient; type objects set it on their runs, in text space)

label: Select Gradient Stop
params: {index: stop index (0 = the start) | null to clear} select a stop of the gradient behind the active proxy (the first selected object's, else the default paint): the stop the Gradient tool's annotator, the Gradient and Color panels and Delete/arrow keys act on → {index}

label: Gradient Presets
params: {} → {presets: [{name, library: the built-in library (theme) it comes from, null for a saved one, builtIn, gradient: {kind, stops, method?, dither?} (as paint.setFill's `gradient`)}]} the Gradient panel's presets: the built-in ones by library, then the saved ones; names are unique

label: Apply Gradient Preset
params: {name: a preset's name (gradient.presets.list), stroke?, item?, ids?|id?, target? (as paint.editGradient)} give the gradient behind the active proxy (or the targeted fill or stroke) the preset's type, stops and method, and a fill its dither, keeping its placement; a solid or no paint becomes the gradient. One undo step, as paint.editGradient → {name, ids: the objects painted (none: only the default changed)}

label: Save Gradient Preset
params: {name?: (default: a new "Gradient Preset N"; unique, any case, and not a built-in preset's)} save the gradient behind the active proxy (paint.toggleActive picks Fill or Stroke) as a preset, kept with the preferences: its type, stops, method and dither (stops linked to a swatch keep their colour, unlinked) → {name}

label: Delete Gradient Preset
params: {name?: a saved preset (default: the saved preset the active proxy's gradient is)} remove a saved preset; built-in presets can't be deleted, and painted art keeps its gradient → {deleted}

label: Make Opacity Mask
params: {ids?, clip?, invert?} the topmost of the selected objects (or of `ids`) becomes the mask of the others (grouped if several; a layer among several stands for its art, so the topmost object of a layer on top is the mask). One object gets an empty mask and enters mask editing: draw the mask, then transparency.stopEditingOpacityMask; one target (an object or a layer) is refused in isolation mode and in pattern editing mode → {id, editing}

label: Release Opacity Mask
params: {id?|ids?} put the mask art back above each masked object (default: the selection, or the object whose mask is being edited, which leaves mask editing)

label: Disable Opacity Mask
params: {id?|ids?} keep the mask but stop applying it

label: Enable Opacity Mask
params: {id?|ids?}

label: Unlink Opacity Mask
params: {id?|ids?} the object moves without its mask

label: Link Opacity Mask
params: {id?|ids?}

label: Opacity Mask Options
params: {id?|ids?, clip?, invert?, disabled?, linked?} change the opacity masks of `ids`, the selection, or the object whose mask is being edited

label: New Opacity Masks Are Clipping
params: {value?} → {value}

label: New Opacity Masks Are Inverted
params: {value?} → {value}

label: Opacity Mask Info
params: {id?|ids?} → [{id, clip, invert, disabled, linked, art}] the opacity masks of `ids`, the selection, or the object whose mask is being edited

label: Transparency Info
params: {id?|ids?} → {ids, opacity: 0..100, blend, isolate, knockout: "on"|"off"|"neutral", knockoutShape, editingMask, pageIsolatedBlending, pageKnockoutGroup} the Transparency panel's values for `ids`, the selection, or the object whose mask is being edited. A value is null where those objects differ (or there are none); editingMask is the id of the object whose mask is being edited, or null; the page values are the document's

label: Page Isolated Blending
params: {value?} make the page an isolated group (default: toggle): blend modes of top-level objects don't blend with what lies under the page; saved with the document and written to PDF → {value}

label: Page Knockout Group
params: {value?} make the page a knockout group (default: toggle): its layers (the contents of neutral layers) hide what they cover instead of showing it through their transparency; saved with the document and written to PDF → {value}

label: New Layer…
params: {name?, top?: bool, below?: bool, color?, template?, locked?, visible?, printable?, preview?, dimImages?} a layer directly above the current layer, at its level (a sublayer beside a current sublayer); `top`: above all layers (Ctrl/Cmd-click the button); `below`: directly below the current layer, at its level (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt-click the button), not with `top`. Options as layer.setProps; refused while an opacity mask is edited (the Layers panel lists only the mask) → {id}

label: New Sublayer…
params: {parent?: layer id (default: the highlighted row's layer, else the current layer), bottom?: bool, name?, …options as layer.new} a sublayer on top of the parent's contents; `bottom`: under the parent's contents, above a clipping layer's clipping path (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt-click the button); refused while an opacity mask is edited → {id}

label: Delete Selection
params: {ids?|id?} delete rows: layers, sublayers, groups or objects with what they hold (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer). The last layer stays → {deleted}

label: Duplicate Selection
params: {ids?|id?} copy rows (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer), each just above its original; a layer's copy is named `<name> copy`. The copies are highlighted → {ids}

label: Set Current Layer
params: {id} click a row: it alone is highlighted, and the layer it is (or the layer it is in) becomes the current layer, where new art goes. Not an undo step → {id, layer}

label: Highlight Rows
params: {ids, mode?: "set"|"add"|"toggle"} highlight Layers panel rows (Shift-click: a range, Ctrl-click: toggle one); the last one's layer becomes current. Not an undo step → {rows}

label: Layer Options…
params: {ids?|id? (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer), name? (with prefs.identifyObjectsBy xmlId: a valid XML ID, stored as the object name), visible?, locked?, template?, printable?, preview?, dimImages?: 0..100|false, color?: index 0..26|"#rrggbb"|preset name} Layer Options; rows that are not layers take name, visible and locked. Template on also locks the layer and dims its images to 50% (unless given); off unlocks it and stops dimming. One undo step

label: Collect in New Layer
params: {ids?} move rows (default: the highlighted rows, else the selected objects) into a new layer where the topmost of them was (a sublayer when they are in a layer), deselecting every selected object left hidden or locked (the key object too) → {id}

label: Select Art
params: {id, add?: bool} the Layers panel's selection column: select the visible, unlocked art of a layer (its sublayers' too), or the object itself; `add` (Shift-click) adds it to the selection, or removes it when it is all selected already → {selected: [..]}

label: Move Rows
params: {ids|id, target, place?: "above"|"below"|"inside" (default inside), copy?: bool} drag rows in the Layers panel: above or below the target row (beside it, in its layer or group), or inside a layer or group (on top of its contents). Layers go only in layers or at the top level, objects in layers and groups; an object placed beside a top-level layer goes inside it. A row never goes into itself; a locked layer or group takes nothing. `copy` (Alt-drag) moves copies. Every selected object left hidden or locked, such as one moved into a hidden layer or group, is deselected (the key object too). One undo step → {ids}

label: Reorder
params: {id, parent?: id (null = top level), index} put a row at `index` (0 = bottom) of `parent` (layers only at the top level or in layers), deselecting every selected object left hidden or locked (the key object too)

label: New Artboard
params: {x?, y?, width?, height?, name?, color?: color (its background color, as artboard.setProps takes it; default: none), showCenterMark?: bool, showCrossHairs?: bool, showVideoSafeAreas?: bool (as artboard.setProps takes them; default false), videoRulerPixelAspectRatio?: number 0.1–10 (as artboard.setProps takes it; default 1)} (default place: right of the last)

label: Delete Artboard
params: {index | indices: [index…]} delete artboards (with their guides) in one step; one is always left, and a locked one is an error

label: Delete Empty Artboards
params: {} delete every artboard with no artwork on it (no object, hidden, locked and template art included, whose visual bounds meet or touch it, clip groups and clipping layers by their members inside the clip; guides don't count), with its guides, in one step; locked artboards stay; when every artboard is empty and none is locked, artboard 1 stays (with a locked one left, artboard 1 can go) → {deleted: [index…]} (the indices before deleting)

label: Artboard Options…
params: {index | artboards: [{index, name?, color?, locked?, showCenterMark?, showCrossHairs?, showVideoSafeAreas?, videoRulerPixelAspectRatio?, x?, y?, width?, height?}…] (several artboards in one undo step, each with its own fields; the art inside each before any of them changes goes with it, and an object inside several goes with the first listed that moves or scales its art), name?, color?: color ("#rrggbb", {c,m,y,k}, … as the paint commands take: the background color the canvas draws the artboard's paper in, multiplied with the Simulate Colored Paper color while that is on; exports and print leave it out) | null (no background color), locked?: bool (the Artboards panel's lock column: a locked artboard keeps its rectangle (a new x, y, width or height is an error unless locked is false), can't be moved, deleted or cut, and Rearrange and Fit to Artwork Bounds leave it as it is; the art on it (each object of a layer or sublayer whose bounds with strokes overlap it, a group as one object) acts as locked art until it is unlocked: clicks, marquees, select.set, select.all and the tools pass over it (art drawn or pasted onto it stays selected and editable until a selection leaves it out or it is moved off the locked artboards), it is deselected, and when another artboard moves or scales it stays unless lockedAndHidden), showCenterMark?: bool (Artboard Options' Show Center Mark: the canvas draws a mark at the artboard's center), showCrossHairs?: bool (Show Cross Hairs: the canvas draws a line from the middle of each side through the center), showVideoSafeAreas?: bool (Show Video Safe Areas: the canvas draws the action-safe area 3.5% and the title-safe area 5% in from each edge, as EBU R 95 sets them; the three are screen-only, as the artboard's edges are: exports and print leave them out), videoRulerPixelAspectRatio?: number 0.1–10 (Video Ruler Pixel Aspect Ratio: the width of one video pixel over its height, which View › Rulers › Show Video Rulers counts the artboard in; default 1, square pixels), x?, y?, width?, height?, moveArt?: bool (default false; a position-only change moves the contained art with its artboard), scaleArt?: bool (Scale Artwork with Artboard: resized, the artboard takes the art fully inside it (locked and hidden art only with lockedAndHidden?: bool, default prefs moveLockedWithArtboard) and its guides from its old rectangle onto the new one, each side by its own ratio; strokes/corners/patterns as object.scale), strokes?: bool, corners?: bool, patterns?: bool (the three as object.scale, for art that moves or scales with the artboard), lockedAndHidden?: bool (locked and hidden art moves along; default: the preference; recorded in the journal so a replay matches)} → null, or with scaleArt {scaled: the art scaled}

label: Fit to Artwork Bounds
params: {index?: n | indices?: [n…] (0-based; the app passes the selected artboards: the Artboard tool's, else the active one; default: the first)} each artboard fits the art on it that shows (with its strokes and effects; hidden objects and layers, guides and template layers don't count), in one undo step: an object counts for every artboard its bounds overlap, and a group or clipping layer counts as one object; an artboard with no art, or a locked one, stays as it is, and the command fails when every artboard it names is locked or none has art

label: Fit to Selected Art
params: {index?: n (0-based; the app passes the active artboard; default: the first)} the artboard fits the selected art (with its strokes); a locked artboard stays as it is (an error when the fit would change it)

label: Make/Release Clipping Mask
params: {id?: layer or group (default: the one highlighted layer or group row, else the one selected group, else the current layer)} make: its top object (a path, compound path or text, which loses its paint) clips the rest and moves to the bottom (new art added on top is clipped); release: it stops clipping, the clipping path stays unpainted → {clip}

label: Target
params: {id, add?: bool (Shift-click: the item joins the selection, or leaves it when all selected; nothing is targeted)} target a layer, group or object as clicking its target circle in the Layers panel does: a layer gets its visible, unlocked art (its sublayers' too) selected and becomes the current layer, and appearance.*, effect.*, transparency.* and the opacity-mask commands without `ids` then act on the layer itself; anything else is selected. Any other selection change ends the targeting (`document.inspect` → target) → {id, selected: [..]}

label: Paste Remembers Layers
params: {on?} (default: toggle) the document option: on, the Paste commands put objects back into the layers they were copied from (by name; a missing one is made on top), off into the current layer; one undo step when it changes (document.inspect → pasteRemembersLayers) → {on}

label: Merge Selected
params: {ids?|id?} (default: the highlighted rows) merge two or more rows into the layer listed (highlighted) last: the other layers' contents and the other rows move into it, keeping their stacking order, and the emptied layers go. Every selected object left hidden or locked, such as one merged into a hidden or locked layer, is deselected (the key object too). One undo step → {id}

label: Flatten Artwork
params: {id?} (default: the highlighted row's top-level layer, else the current one's) move the art of every other visible top-level layer into this one, keeping the stacking order; hidden layers and their art are deleted, template layers stay. Every selected object left hidden or locked, such as one flattened into a locked layer, is deselected (the key object too). One undo step → {id, discarded}

label: Release to Layers (Sequence)
params: {id?: layer or group (default: the highlighted row, else the current layer), build?: bool} each object in it goes into a new sublayer of its own, in stacking order (a group's objects go into sublayers of its layer, where the group was). `build`: Release to Layers (Build), each new sublayer holds copies of the objects up to its own, so the layers add up. One undo step → {ids}

label: Release to Layers (Build)
params: {id?} layer.releaseToLayers with build: true → {ids}

label: Reverse Order
params: {ids?|id?} (default: the highlighted rows) reverse the stacking order of two or more rows that share a layer or group; each keeps the places the others held. One undo step

label: Template
params: {ids?|id?, on?: bool (default: toggle the first)} make layers templates (locked, dimmed, left out of print and export) or ordinary layers again (layer.setProps template) → {on}

label: Hide Others
params: {ids?|id?} hide every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer), which show. One undo step → {count}

label: Show All Layers
params: {} show every layer and sublayer → {count}

label: Outline Others
params: {ids?|id?} turn Preview off (outline view) for every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer), which preview → {count}

label: Preview All Layers
params: {} turn Preview on for every layer and sublayer → {count}

label: Lock Others
params: {ids?|id?} lock every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer), which unlock → {count}

label: Unlock All Layers
params: {} unlock every layer and sublayer → {count}

label: Locate Object
params: {id?} (default: the last selected object) highlight the object's row; the Layers panel opens the layers around it and scrolls to it → {id, ancestry: [layer…, id]}

label: Pencil
params: {points: [[x,y]…] or [[x,y,pressure]…] (pen pressure 0..1: the stroke keeps it, for Calligraphic brushes with Pressure variation; a point without one presses fully), fidelity?: pt (1.5), fit?: bool (true; false: the points are joined by straight segments, as the Pencil previews a stroke with Live curve fitting off), closed?, style?: "pencil"|"brush", fill?: bool, keepSelected?: bool (true: the drawn or continued path is selected; false: it is not, and the rest of the selection stays), extend?: {id, end: "start"|"end"}, connect?: {id, end: "start"|"end"}, redraw?: {id, within?: pt (12)}} fit a freehand stroke → {id}. extend continues the path from that end; with connect, the stroke ends on that end of another path's last open subpath and joins it on, in one path with the extended path's appearance (the other path is removed when nothing of it is left); redraw (Edit Selected Paths) replaces the section of the path between where the stroke starts and ends, each within `within` of one subpath (the shorter way round a closed one), and draws a new path when the stroke doesn't end on it

label: Curvature
params: {points: [{x, y, corner?}], closed?, id?} create (or with id: replace) a path curving through the points → {id}

label: Curvature
params: {id, subpath?, op: "move"|"insert"|"extend"|"close", anchor?, segment?, t?, end?: "start"|"end", from?: "keep"|"smooth"|"corner", corner?, x?, y?} edit a path as the Curvature tool does, its shape kept elsewhere; the anchor edited becomes the direct-selected one → {anchor}. move: anchor to x, y, re-curving only its two segments (a smooth anchor takes the Curvature tool's handles, along the circle through it and its neighbours); insert: a smooth anchor at t on segment, the shape unchanged (with x, y: then moved there); extend: an open subpath goes on from its end (default) or start to a new end at x, y, curving into it unless corner is true; close: an open subpath closes from that end. The old end bends into the new segment as from says: keep its curve (default), smooth through its neighbours, or a corner

label: Delete Anchor Point
params: {id, subpath?, anchor, curvature?} remove one anchor, re-fitting the curve (with curvature: true, the curve where it was follows the remaining anchors, as the Curvature tool curves its points)

label: Remove Anchor Points
params: {} remove the direct-selected anchors without opening their paths, refitting the curve round each; the anchor after each removed one is selected, so running it again goes on along the path → {removedObjects}

label: Convert Anchor Point
params: {id, subpath?, anchor, to: "corner"|"smooth", x?, y?} (smooth with x/y: out handle there, in handle mirrored; without: as the Curvature tool curves a point, along the circle through it and its neighbours, or at an open end one handle into the curve)

label: Reshape Segment
params: {id, subpath?, segment, t, dx, dy, perpendicular?: bool} bend a segment so the point at t moves by (dx, dy); with perpendicular (Shift), both handles stand at right angles to the line between its anchors at one length, and the point at t lies as far from that line as the moved point does

label: Split Path
params: {id, subpath?, segment, t} or {id, subpath?, anchor}: closed paths open there, open paths become two → {ids}

label: Knife
params: {points: [[x,y]…]} cut closed shapes (selected, or all when nothing is selected) along the polyline → {ids}

label: Eraser
params: {points: [[x,y]…] or [[x,y,pressure]…] (pen pressure 0..1), size?: pt (10), sizeMode?: "fixed" (default) | "pressure" (Eraser Tool Options' Size set to Pressure: the tip is size − sizeVariation across where the pen presses lightest and size + sizeVariation where it presses hardest, as path.blob), sizeVariation?: pt (0), angle?: ° (0), roundness?: % (100, kept within 1–100)} erase the stroke of an elliptical tip from paths (selected, or all) → {ids}. The tip is `size` across its long axis, which runs at `angle` counter-clockwise from horizontal; its short axis is `roundness` percent of the long one

label: Path Eraser
params: {points: [[x,y]…], width?: pt (8)} erase the parts of selected paths under the drag → {ids}

label: Smooth
params: {points: [[x,y]…], radius?: pt (12), fidelity?: pt (2.5)} smooth selected paths near the drag → {ids, before, after}

label: Join
params: {points: [[x,y]…], tolerance?: pt (12)} join the open-path endpoints scrubbed over → {id}

label: Blob Brush
params: {points: [[x,y]…] or [[x,y,pressure]…] (pen pressure 0..1), size?: pt (10), sizeMode?: "fixed" (default) | "pressure" (Blob Brush Tool Options' Size set to Pressure: the brush is size − sizeVariation wide at the lightest pen pressure and size + sizeVariation at the heaviest, at least 0.1 pt; a stroke without pressure keeps the size), sizeVariation?: pt (0), angle?: ° (0, kept within −180–180: the tip's long axis counter-clockwise from horizontal, kept on the page along the stroke), roundness?: % (100, kept within 0–100: the tip's short axis in percent of its long one, 100 round; 0 is drawn as 0.1), fidelity?: pt (0.01–100; the brush follows the stroke fitted at this tolerance as path.freehand fits a Pencil stroke, and a higher value gives a smoother shape; without it the brush follows every point), merge?: true, mergeOnlySelection?: bool (false: merge with any touching same-color blob; true: only with selected ones), keepSelected?: bool (false: the drawn or merged path is not selected, and the rest of the selection stays; true: it is selected)} filled brush shape, merged with the topmost touching same-color blob and the touching ones next to it in stacking order in its group or layer → {id}

label: Free Distort
params: {corners: [[x,y]×4] (TL, TR, BR, BL), from?: [x0,y0,x1,y1] (default: selection bounds), ids?} projective warp of anchors and handles

label: Sample Color
params: {color, stroke?: bool (default: whichever proxy is active), ids?, stop?: index, clearStroke?: bool} sample a color into the active fill/stroke (and the selection; `ids: []` changes only the paint default); `clearStroke: true` requires `stroke: false`, `ids: []` and no `stop`, and clears the default stroke after sampling an image into the fill; with `stop`, recolor that stop of the gradient behind the proxy instead (paint.editGradient); in a CMYK document an RGB color is stored as CMYK through the color settings, as paint.setFill stores it

label: Eyedropper Options
params: {sampleSize?: 1|3|5 (pixels square averaged when sampling an image: point, 3×3, 5×5), pickUp?, apply?: {appearance?: {transparency?, fill?: {color?, transparency?, overprint?}, stroke?: {color?, transparency?, overprint?, weight?, cap?, join?, miter?, dash?}}, character?, paragraph?} (bools; a bool for a branch sets all of it)} Eyedropper Options, kept in the preferences: what appearance.copyFrom picks up from the clicked object and applies (only attributes in both trees are copied; every fill and stroke attribute copies the whole appearance stack); {} reads them → the options

label: Move Artboard
params: {index | indices: [index…], dx, dy, moveArt?: bool, copy?: bool, patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles)} move artboards (and the art fully inside them; locked and hidden art, and art also on another locked artboard, only with prefs moveLockedWithArtboard), several in one step (an error when one is locked); `copy` (Alt-drag) leaves them and moves copies, which start unlocked → {index (the first), indices: the artboards moved or the copies, moved: the art moved or the copies}

label: Apply Effect
params: {effect: id (see effect.list, e.g. "stylize.dropShadow", "distort.roughen", "warp.arc", or "plugin.<id>" for an installed effect plug-in), params?: {…} (missing keys take the dialog defaults), item?: appearance item index|null (apply to that fill/stroke only; omitted: the Appearance panel's active item, else the whole object), ids?|id?: [..] (layers too), target?: "object"|"contents" (contents: the objects inside groups and layers)} append a live effect to each selected object's appearance (a group's or layer's apply to its members as one piece: one combined shadow; a Pathfinder effect, which combines a group's contents, groups several loose selected objects first, in the same undo step) → {ids, index, item, grouped?}

label: Effects
params: {ids?|id?: object ids (default: the selection), target?: "object"|"contents"} → {catalog: [{id, label, menu, params, defaults, raster, lengths: {always, absolute (while relative is false)} (distance params Scale Strokes & Effects scales)}] (installed effect plug-ins last: id plugin.<plug-in id>, menu Effect › Plug-ins), applied: [{id, effects, items: [{index, kind: fill|stroke, effects}]}], activeItem} for the selection

label: Remove Effect
params: {index: int (position in the effect list), item?: appearance item index|null (that fill/stroke's effects; omitted: the active item, else the object's), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents", aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first target's stack: each other target edits its equal one, as the Appearance panel does for a mixed selection)} → {ids}

label: Effect Options
params: {index: int, params?: {…} (merged into the current parameters), warpStyle?: string (an existing Warp style suffix, e.g. arc or flag; changes only an applied Warp in place), visible?: bool, item?: appearance item index|null (as effect.remove), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents", aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first target's stack: each other target edits its equal one, as the Appearance panel does for a mixed selection)} → {ids}

label: 3D Lighting Preset
params: {index: int, preset: standard|diffuse|topLeft|right, item?: appearance item index|null (omitted: the active item, else the object's), ids?|id?: [..], target?: object|contents, aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first target's stack: each other target edits its equal one, as the Appearance panel does for a mixed selection)} replace an applied 3D effect's light rig and ambient with an original lighting preset; preserve shading, geometry and view; all targets must have a 3D effect at index; one undo step → {ids}

label: Expand Appearance
params: {ids?|id?: [..], target?} turn each object's appearance into objects: every fill and stroke becomes an object of its own (a stroke stays a stroke, with its weight, dashes, arrowheads and width profile, on its own copy of the path, which object.expand or object.path.outlineStroke outline; brushed strokes become their brush art) grouped in paint order under the object's id and transparency, geometry effects are baked, raster effects become an embedded image (shadows and outer glows below the art; blur, feather and inner glow replace it; an object whose only raster effect is its own Rasterize becomes the image object.rasterize makes with the effect's options), type with effects or fills of its own is outlined; Crop Marks become a group of the object and its marks; Vector Halftone (addon.color.halftone) becomes a group of its dot paths, one per ink; a group's or layer's own fills and strokes become objects among its members, which are expanded too. An outlined frame of threaded text leaves its thread with the text it shows, and a frame kept as type in a group stays in its thread. Hidden fills, strokes and effects are dropped. Enabled when a selected or targeted object's appearance isn't basic (`ids` then pick which objects) → {ids, warning? (an image in the art couldn't be decoded, as object.rasterize says)}

label: Duplicate Effect
params: {index: int, item?: appearance item index|null (as effect.remove), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents", aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first target's stack: each other target edits its equal one, as the Appearance panel does for a mixed selection)} insert a copy of the effect right after it → {ids}

label: Move Effect
params: {from: int (position in the source list), to: int (its position in the destination list afterwards), fromItem?: appearance item index|null (the source list: that fill/stroke's effects, null the object's; omitted: the active item, else the object's), toItem?: item index|null (the destination list; default: the source list), copy?: bool (copy instead of move, as Alt-dragging the row), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents", aligned?: bool (refused when the targets' appearances differ)} reorder an effect or move it between the object and its fills/strokes, as one undo step → {ids, index, item}

label: Unite
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

label: Minus Front
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

label: Intersect
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

label: Exclude
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

label: Divide
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

label: Trim
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

label: Merge
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

label: Crop
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

label: Outline
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

label: Minus Back
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

label: Trap…
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), thickness?: pt 0.01..5000 (0.25; how far the lighter colour reaches into the darker one across vertical edges), heightWidth?: % 1..1000 (100; the reach across horizontal edges as a percentage of the vertical one), tintReduction?: % 0..100 (40; the trap paints the lighter colour at this percentage of its tint), trapsWithProcessColor?: bool (false; a swatch (spot) colour's trap is painted with its CMYK process equivalent), reverseTraps?: bool (false; the darker colour spreads into the lighter one, except a rich black)} adds overprinting traps where the selected objects' visible areas of different solid colours meet, grouped directly above the topmost selected object and selected; the objects stay as they are → {ids}

label: Pathfinder Options…
params: {precision?: pt 0.001..10 (0.01; how closely the Pathfinder operations follow the paths: results are refit to within it and pieces thinner than it are dropped), removeRedundantPoints?: bool (false; the results lose the anchors that don't change their shape), removeUnpainted?: bool (false; Divide and Outline leave out the pieces of objects with no fill)} Pathfinder Options, kept in the preferences and used by every later Shape Mode and Pathfinder operation (not Trap); {} reads them → the options

label: Outline Stroke
params: {} replace stroked paths with filled outlines → {ids}

label: Offset Path…
params: {offset: pt (negative insets), joins?: "miter"|"round"|"bevel", miterLimit?: 4} → {ids} (new objects above the originals)

label: Simplify…
params: {tolerance?: pt (1), level?: 0..100 (the Simplify slider, in place of tolerance: 0 fewest anchor points, 50 is 1 pt, every 10 levels halves or doubles it), auto?: bool (Auto-Simplify: the lowest level whose tolerance is at most 1/400 of the selection's longer side, or 100 when that side is under 12.5 pt), cornerAngle?: deg (30), straightLines?: bool, wholePaths?: bool (false: a path with segments direct-selected, or between direct-selected anchors, simplifies only each run of them between its end anchors, which stay as they are, and keeps the runs selected; true simplifies those paths whole)} → {ids, before, after} anchor counts, and the level used with level or auto

label: Smooth…
params: {level?: 0..100 (50; the Smooth slider: 0 minimum smoothing, the path staying within 0.1% of its longer side, 100 maximum: smoothed along its length by up to 5% of it and refitted with curves within up to 2.5% of it, corners kept only where the path turns back, never with more anchor points), auto?: bool (Auto-Smooth: level 50), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} smooth each path under the objects, compound path members included, as one undo step; without ids, a path with anchor points or segments direct-selected smooths only the sections between them, which stay selected → {ids, before, after} anchor counts, and the level used

label: Divide Objects Below
params: {} cut the objects below with the selected path (which is removed) → {ids}

label: Split Into Grid…
params: {rows?: 2, columns?: 2, gutter?: pt (12; rowGutter?, columnGutter?: one of the two), totalHeight?, totalWidth?: pt (the grid's size; the selected paths' when left out), height?, width?: pt (each row's and column's size, which then sets the total), addGuides?: false (ruler guides along the row and column edges)} one grid of rectangles over the selected paths replaces them, painted as the topmost one → {ids, guides: count}

label: Clean Up…
params: {strayPoints?: true, unpaintedObjects?: true, emptyTextPaths?: true} → {removed}

label: Make Compound Shape
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), mode?: "add"|"subtract"|"intersect"|"exclude" (default add; Alt-clicking a Shape Mode button gives its mode)} the two or more selected objects (paths, compound paths, groups, compound shapes, type) become the members of one compound shape, each with the shape mode, in their stacking order where the frontmost was: it draws as the area they make from the backmost up (open paths closed), painted with the appearance and transparency of the topmost member in Add, Intersect or Exclude mode (with every member in Subtract, the backmost), and the members stay editable (Direct Selection, Layers panel, isolation mode) → {id}

label: Shape Mode
params: {mode: "add"|"subtract"|"intersect"|"exclude", ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} the members of compound shapes that the selected objects are or are in take the shape mode (what clicking a Shape Mode button does with members selected); the backmost member's mode doesn't change the shape → {ids}

label: Release Compound Shape
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} the selected compound shapes (and those holding the selected objects) become their members again, as they were before Make Compound Shape, selected → {ids}

label: Expand Compound Shape
params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} the selected compound shapes (and those holding the selected objects) become the path, or compound path, of the area they draw, painted as they are, selected → {ids}

label: Vertical
params: {ids?|id?} set vertical writing

label: Horizontal
params: {ids?|id?} set horizontal writing

label: Create Outlines
params: {} convert the selected text to groups of compound paths (one per glyph); a frame of threaded text leaves its thread with the text it shows → {ids}

label: Scale Text Attributes
params: {ids?|id?} bake each selected type object's transform scale into its character sizes (leading, baseline shift and horizontal scale included), leaving rotation and position in the affine → {ids, changed}

label: Optical Margin Alignment
params: {ids?|id?, on?: bool} turn Optical Margin Alignment on or off for the selected type and every frame of its threads (on omitted: the opposite of the first object's setting): in every paragraph of point and area type, quotation marks, hyphens, full stops and commas at a line's start or end hang wholly outside the margin there; asterisks, tildes, ellipses, en and em dashes, colons and semicolons hang by half; and A, V, W, Y, v, w and y hang by a tenth of their advance; a left-aligned line hangs at its left margin, a right-aligned line hangs at its right margin, and centered and justified lines hang at both; Auto aligns a right-to-left line at its right; type on a path hangs at the start bracket when its line is placed there, hangs at the end bracket when the line is placed there, and hangs at both when it is centered → {on, ids}

label: System Layout
params: {on?: bool} turn System Layout on or off for the document (on omitted: the opposite of the document's setting) and every text object in it. On, each character that takes any space advances by a whole number of points, at least one, so small type does not run together; a character with no width stays at none. Off (the default, and what a document from before it reads as), spacing uses fractions of a point. New point, area and path type inherits the document's setting → {on}

label: Fractional Widths
params: {ids?|id?, on?: bool} turn Fractional Widths on or off for the selected type and every frame of its threads (on omitted: the opposite of the first object's setting). On (the default, and what a document from before it reads as), spacing between characters uses fractions of a point. Off, each character that takes any space advances by a whole number of points, at least one, so small type does not run together; a character with no width stays at none. The setting is the whole type object, not a range of characters → {on, ids}

label: Set Text
params: {id?|ids?, text} replace the contents of text objects (keeps the first run's style) → {ids, overflow?: [id…] (area type and type on a path whose text no longer fits; left out when all fits)}

label: Area Type Options…
params: {ids?|id?, width?: pt, height?: pt, rows?, columns?, gutter?: pt, inset?: pt, firstBaseline?: ascent|capHeight|xHeight|leading|fixed, firstBaselineMin?: pt, verticalAlign?: top|center|bottom|justify, flow?: columns|rows (Text Flow: down each column's rows, then across, the default; or across each row's columns, then down), fit?: none|autoHeight|shrinkText, fitMinPercent?: 10..100, …the keys of its own reply (it can be passed back; the values it only reports are ignored)} set the selected area type's options; width and height size the type area from its top-left corner, along the type's own axes, and the text reflows at its size (with fit autoHeight, Auto Size, the frame's height follows the text after every edit and height is ignored; setting the height by hand turns it off); fit shrinkText scales overflowing text down (size, leading, baseline shift) by the largest factor down to fitMinPercent % (default 50) that makes it fit (none given: query) → the first object's options, plus overflow (the text doesn't fit its frame) and fitScale (Shrink Text's factor, 1 unshrunk)

label: Reshape Type Area
params: {id, anchors: [[subpath, anchor]…], dx, dy} or {items: [{id, anchors}…], dx, dy} move anchors of area type's frame (the type area) by dx, dy points, with their handles; the text reflows at its size, through its thread too (what Direct Selection does dragging a frame corner or edge, or the frame anchors its marquee selected, and the arrow keys nudging those); with items, every listed frame moves in one step

label: Reshape Type Path
params: {id, anchors: [[subpath, anchor]…], dx, dy} move anchors of type on a path's path by dx, dy points, with their handles; the start and end brackets keep their fractions of the path and the text reflows along it (what Direct Selection does dragging an anchor of the path)

label: Fit Headline
params: {ids?|id?} track the first line of area type so it fills the frame width → {tracking}

label: Character
params: {ids?|id?, font?, style? (font alone: the style is kept when the new family has it, else its closest), size?: pt, leading?: pt|"auto", tracking?: 1/1000 em, justify?: "auto" (the start of each paragraph's direction)|"left"|"center"|"right"|"justifyAll", fill?: colour, keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), features?: ["dlig", "-liga", …] OpenType, start?: byte, end?: byte} (size/leading are document points after object scaling; with a range: the character attributes style that range and justify the paragraphs it touches; without: all the text) → {ids, overflow?: [id…] (area type and type on a path whose text no longer fits; left out when all fits), warning?: text (the font or style set isn't available: its type is drawn in the fallback font or the family's closest style)}

label: Ruby…
params: {ids?|id?, start?: byte, end?: byte, text?: reading, position?: above|below (vertical type: right|left), align?: start|center|end, size?: 1–100 (percent of the base text's size, default 50), overhang?: bool (default true), remove?: bool} set the ruby (furigana) over the selected text's bytes in `start..end` (without them: all its text): the reading over the base characters, above them in horizontal type and right of them in vertical type; `remove` takes the ruby off the range instead → {ids, ruby: [{start, end, text, position, align, sizePercent, overhang}…] (the first object's ruby)}

label: All Artwork Above
params: {} lock objects in the same layer that are above and overlap the selection, deselecting every selected object left locked or hidden (the key object too); in isolation mode, lock the selected objects and the objects above them inside the isolated object → {count}

label: Other Layers
params: {} lock every layer that holds no selected object; in isolation mode, change nothing and return a count of 0 → {count}

label: Unselected Artwork
params: {} lock unselected artwork in one undo step, including unselected members of partly selected groups, clipping groups and compound paths, and guides while Lock Guides is on; hidden art and art on locked layers stay unlocked; a selected layer's art counts as selected; in isolation, only art inside the isolated object is affected; object.unlockAll unlocks locked art document-wide, or inside the isolated object in isolation mode → {count}

label: All Artwork Above
params: {} hide objects in the same layer that are above and overlap the selection, deselecting every selected object left hidden or locked (the key object too); in isolation mode, hide the selected objects and the objects above them inside the isolated object → {count}

label: Other Layers
params: {} hide every layer that holds no selected object; in isolation mode, change nothing and return a count of 0 → {count}

label: Unselected Artwork
params: {} hide, in one undo step, every object select.all takes that is not selected and holds no selected object; in a group that holds one it hides the other members one by one, and a clip group, compound path or other object that holds one stays as it is; the objects of a selected layer count as selected; while Lock Guides is on, guide paths count as selected and stay as they are; in isolation mode, only art inside the isolated object is affected; object.showAll shows them again → {count}

label: Transform Each…
params: {scaleH?: % (100), scaleV?: % (100), moveH?: pt, moveV?: pt (down = +), rotate?: deg (counter-clockwise), reflectX?: bool (flip left-right, as Reflect X in the Transform Each dialog), reflectY?: bool (flip top-bottom, as Reflect Y), random?: bool, seed?: n, reference?: 0..8 (9-point grid, 4 = centre), copy?: bool, strokes?: bool (Scale Strokes & Effects), corners?: bool (Scale Corners; both default to the preferences), objects?: bool (Transform Objects, default true; false: the art stays and, with patterns, only its pattern tiles transform), patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns; default: prefs transformPatternTiles)} transform every selected object about its own reference point → {ids}

label: Reset Bounding Box
params: {} square the bounding box of the selected objects to the page again after a rotation (their geometry stays; one undo step, none when no box is rotated) → {changed: objects reset}

label: Rasterize…
params: {ppi?, background?: transparent|white|black|"#rrggbb", antiAlias?: none|art|type (text snapped to pixels)|bool, padding?|addAround?: pt (0–1000), colorModel?: "rgb"|"cmyk"|"grayscale"|"bitmap", clippingMask?: bool (a clip group with the art's outline)} replace the selection with an embedded image (PNG; in a CMYK document with its own colour model, a CMYK image of the art's inks, its transparency as its opacity mask); each defaults to document.rasterEffectsSettings; a frame of threaded text that is rasterized leaves its thread with the text it shows → {id (the image, or its clip group), width, height, warning?: "an image couldn't be decoded and is missing from the picture" (as raster exports say)}

label: Create Object Mosaic…
params: {columns=10, rows=10 (whole numbers, kept within 1..1000), width?, height? (new size in pt; default the image's), spacingX=0, spacingY=0 (pt between tiles), gray?: bool, deleteRaster?: bool} a group of rectangles coloured by the selected image's average tile colours → {id, tiles}

label: Crop Image
params: {rect?: [x, y, width, height] | trim?: true (to the pixels that aren't fully transparent, pixel for pixel; an image with none to cut is left as it is, trimmed: false)} crop the selected image (default: to the artboard it sits on) → {id, width, height, trimmed? (with trim), warning? (without trim: the image couldn't be decoded, as object.rasterize says)}

label: Mask
params: {} clip the selected image with a rectangle around it (its own outline, rotated with it) and select that clipping path, whose handles then crop it; one undo step → {id: the clip group, path: the clipping path}

label: Create Trim Marks
params: {style?: "roman"|"japanese" (default: the japaneseCropMarks preference; japanese: double lines at the trim and bleed edges plus centre marks), allArtboards?: bool (default: true when nothing is selected), offset?: pt (9, roman), length?: pt (18), bleed?: pt (8.5, japanese), weight?: pt (0.3)} trim marks stroked in [Registration] (printing on every plate) around the selection, or around every artboard, one group each, as one undo step → {id: the first group, ids}

label: Convert to Shape
params: {} turn paths that are rectangles (any rotation) or axis-aligned ellipses into live shapes → {converted}

label: Convert to Artboards
params: {} turn each selected object's bounds into a new artboard (the objects are removed) → {artboards}

label: Rearrange All Artboards…
params: {layout?: gridByRow|gridByColumn|row|column (gridByRow; byColumn?: true is gridByColumn), order?: leftToRight|rightToLeft (leftToRight: right-to-left mirrors the order along the rows), columns?: n (2; the rows for gridByColumn; row and column ignore it), spacing?: pt (20), moveArtwork?: true (each object of a layer or sublayer moves with the artboard its center is on; locked and hidden art, and art on a locked artboard, only with prefs moveLockedWithArtboard), patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles), byColumn?: bool (an older way to ask for layout gridByColumn)} lay the artboards out in their order, the grid's top-left at the first artboard's; a locked artboard stays where it is → {artboards, rows, columns}

label: Make
params: {ids?, steps?: n | distance?: pt | smooth?: bool, orientation?: page|path (default: the Blend Options set with nothing selected, else smooth colour and page), starts?: [anchor index | null, …] (per object of `ids`, else of the selection in paint order: the anchor of its first subpath the blend starts from; an open path's last anchor runs it the other way), spacing?: smooth|steps|distance (with value), value?: n, easingType?: easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut|easeOutIn, ramp?: pct (0..100), colorShift?: pct (-100..100; 0: even)} blend the selected objects (paint order) into a live blend; a blend among them takes the others in as more key objects (keeping its options, name and transparency) instead of nesting → {id}

label: Release
params: {} release the selected blends: the key objects come back and the spine stays as a path with no fill or stroke, below them; a blend with a name, opacity, blend mode, isolation, opacity mask or appearance of its own comes back as a group keeping them (and its knockout) → {ids (the keys), spines: [ids], groups: [ids]}

label: Blend Options…
params: {spacing?: smooth|steps|distance, value?: n, steps?: n, distance?: pt, orientation?: page|path, smooth?: bool, easingType?: easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut|easeOutIn, ramp?: pct, colorShift?: pct} set the options of the selected blends; easingType chooses the distribution, ramp sets its strength (0..100; 0 = even), colorShift (-100..100; 0 = even) shifts colours independently of shape/position easing (omitted ones keep their value; out of range is an error); with no blend selected, the options new blends start with (spacing and orientation only; a tool setting, not an undo step) → {defaults?: true}

label: Expand
params: {} replace the selected blends by groups of their keys and steps, each keeping the blend's id, name, transparency (knockout and isolation included), opacity mask and appearance → {ids}

label: Replace Spine
params: {} use the selected path as the spine of the selected blend (the path is consumed)

label: Reverse Spine
params: {} reverse the order of the key objects along the spine

label: Blend Info
params: {} the options of the first selected blend, else those new blends start with → {target: blend|defaults, id?, spacing: smooth|steps|distance, steps, distance, orientation: page|path, easingType?: easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut|easeOutIn, ramp?: pct, colorShift?: pct, keys?: [ids], starts?: [anchor|null], spine?: {anchors: [{x, y, in: [x, y], out: [x, y]}], closed, keyAnchors: [anchor each key sits on] | null (keys spread evenly: a spine from Replace Spine), explicit: false for the straight lines between the key centres}}

label: Move Spine Point
params: {id? (default: the selected blend), anchor: index, x, y, handle?: in|out, independent?: bool} move a point of the blend's spine (its handles along), or with `handle` place that handle's end at (x, y) (a smooth point keeps the other handle in line unless `independent`). A key object sitting on the point moves with it. The first edit turns the straight spine into a path

label: Convert Anchor Point
params: {id? (default: the selected blend), anchor: index, to: smooth|corner, x?, y?} convert a blend spine point: dragging a corner creates symmetric smooth handles, clicking a point with handles retracts both. Without x/y, smooth uses the neighbouring spine points

label: Reshape Spine Segment
params: {id? (default: the selected blend), segment: index, t: 0..1, dx, dy, perpendicular?: bool} bend a segment of the blend's spine so its point at t moves by (dx, dy), as path.reshapeSegment bends a path's (perpendicular too): a straight spine turns into a curve (#1111)

label: Add Spine Point
params: {id? (default: the selected blend), x, y} add a point to the blend's spine where it passes nearest (x, y) → {anchor}

label: Delete Spine Point
params: {id? (default: the selected blend), anchor: index} delete a point of the blend's spine that no key object sits on

label: Reverse Front to Back
params: {} reverse the stacking order of the selected blends

label: Make with Warp…
params: {ids?, style?: arc|arcLower|arcUpper|arch|bulge|shellLower|shellUpper|flag|wave|fish|rise|fisheye|inflate|squeeze|twist (arc), bend?: % -100..100 (50), h?: horizontal distortion % -100..100 (0), v?: vertical distortion % (0), horizontal?: bool (true) | orientation?: horizontal|vertical, horizontalDistortion?: as h, verticalDistortion?: as v} envelope the selected objects with a warp (Envelope Options from object.envelope.options with nothing selected) → {id}

label: Make with Mesh…
params: {ids?, rows?: 1..50 (4), cols?: 1..50 (4), columns?: as cols} envelope the selected objects with a mesh of rows × cols patches → {id}

label: Make with Top Object
params: {ids?} the topmost selected path becomes the envelope of the others → {id}

label: Reset with Warp…

label: Convert to Text
params: {ids?|id?, start?: byte, end?: byte} (Type › Bullets and Numbering › Convert to Text: the paragraphs of the selected type, or of `ids`, or those a start/end range touches) the marker of each list paragraph becomes characters of its text: the bullet, or the number and its period as the paragraph showed it, then a tab, at the start of the paragraph in the marker's font, size and color; the list is turned off. When the marker's tab went to the left indent, the paragraph gets a left-aligned tab stop without a leader there, in place of any stop there, which keeps the text after the tab where it started; when it went to a tab stop and a stop there or past it has a leader or is not left-aligned, or a right, center or decimal stop lies between the marker and that place, the paragraph gets a left-aligned stop without a leader where the marker's tab ended, in place of any stop there and of those right, center and decimal stops before it (past the left indent only in a paragraph with no tab of its own). In threaded type the numbers are those counted through the story's frames, and a paragraph that continues into a later frame is converted where its text starts. An empty list paragraph has no marker and only leaves the list. A paragraph with no direction set gets the direction it ran in when the characters would change it (a letter or roman numeral before right-to-left text). With the Every-line Composer, a paragraph with a tab is broken line by line, so a converted paragraph can break its lines at other places. While the Type tool edits, its typing ends first and its anchor and caret move past the characters inserted at or before them; in threaded type, when the caret's character moved to another frame, the tool edits that frame, which becomes the selection when it was not selected. params: {} choose the Intertwine tool for the selected Intertwine group (Esc or Enter goes back to the tool before)

label: Release
params: {} give the objects of the selected Intertwine groups back as they were made, dropping the arranged areas → {ids}

label: Arrange Intertwine Area
params: {id?: Intertwine group (default: the selected one), at?: [x,y] (the overlap area under this point, as a click picks it) | area?: [[x,y]…] (a closed polygon drawn around overlap areas: every area whose inside it encloses), order?: toggle|front|forward|backward|back (toggle: the object drawn right below the top comes to the front, so two objects swap; forward and backward move an object one place up or down among the objects in that area; the others keep their order there), member?: id (front, forward, backward and back: the object to move; default: front and forward move the object right below the top, back and backward the top one)} → {count: areas changed (an area already in that order is not changed, and with none changed there is no undo step), top: [id of the object now on top in each changed area]}

label: Attach
params: {path?: id of the path to attach to (without it: choose the Objects on Path tool, whose click on a path attaches the selection to it), ids?: the objects to attach (default: the selection; the path is left out of it), pivot?: 0-8 (the reference point of each object that attaches to the path, row by row from the top left; default: the Objects on Path tool's Pivot, 4, the center, until its options change it), rotate?: degrees counter-clockwise from upright on the path (default: the tool's Rotate, 0 until its options change it)} put the objects and the path in an Objects on Path group: the path at the bottom, the objects spread evenly along it from its first anchor (the last one at the end of an open path) in their order on the canvas, column by column from left to right and top to bottom in each column, each turned to follow the path; editing the path moves them → {id}

label: Objects on Path Options
params: {ids?: Objects on Path groups or objects in them (default: the selection), pivot?: 0-8 (the reference point of each object that attaches to the path, row by row from the top left; 4: the center), rotate?: degrees counter-clockwise from upright on the path} set how the objects of the groups attach → {ids}

label: Expand
params: {ids?: Objects on Path groups or objects in them (default: the selection)} make the groups plain groups of the path and the objects where they are → {ids}

label: Get Preferences
params: {key?} → the value of one preference (or preference group: eyedropper), or {prefs: {…all…}}

label: Set Preference
params: {key, value} or {values: {key: value, …}} set preferences (validated; see prefs.list; lengths in pt or strings with a unit; unitsGeneral also sets the active document's units, one undo step; the eyedropper group takes a partial object, as eyedropper.setOptions)

label: Reset Preferences
params: {category?} reset one category (or everything) to defaults

label: List Preferences
params: {} → [{key, category, section, label, kind, value, …}] every preference

label: Width Point
params: {id, t: 0..1 (fraction of the path length), left, right: side widths in pt, index?: width point to edit or move, adjustAdjoining?: bool (the nearest points either side change their widths in proportion, using the sampled widths for a new point)} → {index}. Without index a point already at t is replaced; a point moved onto another one's t joins it as a discontinuous point (on the side it came from), so the width steps there. Creates a uniform profile first if needed

label: Delete Width Point
params: {id, index | indices: [..]} remove width points (removing the last one leaves a uniform stroke)

label: Copy Width Point
params: {id, index: the width point to copy, t: 0..1 where the copy goes} → {index} (Alt-drag with the Width tool). Landing on another point makes a discontinuous point, as a stroke.widthPoint.set move does

label: Width Profile
params: {ids?|id?, points: [[t, left, right]…] (width factors, 1 = the stroke weight) | null = uniform}

label: Liquify
params: {tool: warp|twirl|pucker|bloat|scallop|crystallize|wrinkle, points: [[x,y,pressure?]…] (the brush stroke; pen pressure 0..1, default 1), diameter?|width?, height? (pt, default 100), angle?, intensity? (0..1 or %), usePressure?: bool (each point's pressure is the intensity there), detail? (1..10), simplify?: 0..100, simplifyOn?: bool (default true; both for warp, twirl, pucker, bloat), rate? (twirl °), complexity? (0..15), horizontal?, vertical? (wrinkle, 0..1 or %), affectAnchors?, affectIn?, affectOut?: bool (scallop, crystallize, wrinkle; default true), ids?|id? (default: selection, else every path the brush touches)}

label: Puppet Warp
params: {id?|ids? (default: selection), pins: [[x,y]…] (current pin positions), moved: [[x,y]…] (targets, same length), angles?: [deg|null…] (same length: the turn the art takes around each pin, as Alt-dragging around a pin does; null leaves it free), expand?: pt, rest?: bool, auto?: bool (as object.puppetWarp.pins reports; ignored)} as-rigid-as-possible mesh warp of anchors and handles. rest: true = the Puppet Warp tool's pins: `pins` are points on the shape the pins started from (object.puppetWarp.pins), each must be on its mesh, the warp replaces the previous one instead of adding to it, and the pins are kept with the document for Undo (an empty list removes them all, leaving the art as it is)

label: Puppet Warp Pins
params: {id?|ids? (default: selection), expand?: pt} → {ids, pins, moved, angles, expand, rest: true, auto} the Puppet Warp pins on the art: pins = where each sits on the shape they started from, moved = where it is now, angles = the turn it holds (deg, null = free); auto: none placed yet (the tool's automatic pins: the centre and the end of each limb). Change moved/angles (or add/remove pins) and pass it back to object.puppetWarp

label: Define Perspective Grid
params: {kind?: 1|2|3, origin?: [x,y], horizon?, vpLeft?, vpRight?, vpVertical?: [x,y], distance?, cell?, extent?, height?, visible?, plane?, leftOffset?, rightOffset?, groundOffset?: pt (planes moved along their normals), reproject?: bool, …the other fields of the grid as its reply lists them} merge into the document's grid. Objects in perspective stay where they are, as in the reference app; with reproject they move with the grid (each keeps its place on its plane)

label: Perspective Grid Preset
params: {kind: 1|2|3 (its normal view) | name: a preset (see perspective.presets.list)} reset the grid to the preset fitted to the first artboard (and show it; attached objects stay attached)

label: Show Perspective Grid
params: {visible?: bool} (no param toggles). View state: not an undo step

label: Active Perspective Plane
params: {plane: left|right|ground|none} Plane Switching widget. View state: not an undo step

label: Attach to Active Plane
params: {ids?|id?, plane?: left|right|ground (default: the active plane)} project the objects onto the plane

label: Release with Perspective
params: {ids?|id?} detach from the grid (geometry unchanged)

label: Move in Perspective
params: {ids?|id?, from: [x,y], to: [x,y], plane?, copy?: bool (move copies, as Alt-dragging does), perpendicular?: bool (move along the plane's normal instead, as pressing 5 while dragging does), snap?: bool (default: View › Perspective Grid › Snap to Grid), constrain?: bool (default false; constrain each in-plane move to its plane's nearest axis or 45° diagonal)} slide objects within their own planes (unattached objects attach to `plane`/the active plane first); snapping pulls the nearer edge of the first plane's joint bounds toward a gridline within a quarter cell while preserving the constrained direction; Transform Again repeats it

label: Draw in Perspective
params: {command: shape.* id, params, plane?, snap?: bool (default: Snap to Grid), at?: [x, y] (a point of the plane the shape lies on, as the tool gives it)} run a shape command and attach the result to the plane (snapping its corners to gridlines within a quarter cell)

label: Transform in Perspective
params: {ids?|id?, matrix: [a,b,c,d,e,f] (affine map in plane coordinates, points: u along the plane, v up or away), depth?: pt to move along the plane's normal (default 0), copy?: bool, plane?} transform objects within their own planes (Perspective Selection tool handles; unattached objects attach to `plane`/the active plane first); Transform Again repeats it → {ids}

label: Nudge in Perspective
params: {dx, dy: arrow direction (-1, 0 or 1), big?: bool (×10), copy?: bool} move the selection in perspective by the keyboard increment, as the arrow keys do with the Perspective Selection tool → {ids}

label: Move Plane
params: {plane?: left|right|ground (default: the active plane), offset?: pt (where along its normal; 0 is its place in the grid's definition) | by?: pt, objects?: none|move|copy (default none: the objects on the plane stay; move: they move with it, as Shift-dragging a plane widget does; copy: copies of them do, as Alt-dragging does)} → {plane, offset, ids}

label: Move Plane to Match Object
params: {id? (default: the first selected object)} move the plane the object is attached to onto the object and make it the active plane → {plane, offset}

label: Edit Text
params: {id? (default: the selected type)} Object › Perspective › Edit Text: show type in perspective flat where it is drawn, in isolation mode, to edit it (text.* commands, the Type tool); exiting isolation (object.exitIsolation, Esc) projects it again; refused while an opacity mask is edited → {id}

label: Invert
params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} invert the active proxy's colours of the selection (or ids; groups recolour their contents) keeping each colour's model, as edit.colors.invert does; the Appearance panel's active fill/stroke item (appearance.setActiveItem) is inverted instead when it is of that kind and no ids are given; with nothing selected, invert the default → {changed}

label: Complement
params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} replace the active proxy's colours by their complements ((highest + lowest) − each component, over RGB or CMY; grey unchanged) keeping each colour's model; honours the Appearance panel's active item as paint.invert does; with nothing selected, the default → {changed}

label: Apply Last Color
params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} apply the last solid colour used (paint.recent lastColor) to the active proxy of the selection and the default → {objects} (as paint.setFill)

label: Apply Last Gradient
params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} apply the last gradient used (paint.recent lastGradient), fitted to each object, to the active proxy of the selection and the default → {objects} (as paint.setFill)

label: Recent Colors
params: {} → {colors: [{hex, color}] newest first (fed by every paint command and the eyedropper), lastColor: {hex, color}, lastGradient: gradient paint}

label: Fill and Stroke
params: {} → {fill, stroke: the paints the Fill/Stroke proxies show (the Appearance panel's active item for the proxy of its kind, else the first selected object's, a group's first painted object's, type: its first run's; else the defaults for new art), fillActive, fillMixed, strokeMixed: the selected objects' (or a selected group's contents') fills (strokes) differ, shown as a "?" proxy}

label: Overprint
params: {fill?: bool, stroke?: bool, item?: appearance item index|null, ids?|id?, target?: "object"|"contents"} make fills and/or strokes overprint (Overprint Preview, Separations Preview) or knock out: item's, else every fill or stroke of the painted objects (groups: their contents; type: its characters too). Without item and ids, the Appearance panel's active item stands in when it is of that kind → {changed: objects}

label: Attributes
params: {ids?|id?, item?, target?: "object"|"contents"} → {ids, overprintFill, overprintStroke, showCenter, imageMap: "none"|"rectangle"|"polygon", url, note, fillRule: "nonZero"|"evenOdd" (of the paths and compound paths in them), reversed (their subpaths run counter-clockwise on screen: Reverse Path Direction On), recentUrls: [newest first]} the Attributes panel's values for `ids` or the selection, overprint aimed as object.setOverprint aims; a value is null where they differ (or nothing has a fill, stroke or path)

label: Swatch Libraries
params: {} → {libraries: [{id, name, category: "builtIn"|"gradients"|"user" (User Defined: the library files in the user library folder, rescanned now)|"loaded" (swatch.library.load), count, path?}], userFolder} every library the library panel opens, in menu order

label: Swatch Library
params: {library: id or name} → {id, name, category, swatches: [{name, kind, group, global, spot, color?, hex?, gradient?}] (as swatch.list), groups: [{name, swatches: [names]}]}

label: Add to Swatches
params: {library: id or name, names?: [swatch or colour group names in the library] (default: all of it; a group comes as a colour group, a single swatch ungrouped), apply?: "fill"|"stroke" (also apply the first one to the selection and the defaults, as paint.setFill / paint.setStroke), focus?: true (with apply: false keeps the active proxy)} copy library swatches into the document as one undo step. A swatch the document already has (same name and paint) isn't added again; a name taken by another swatch gets a number ("Clay 1 2") → {library, added: [names in the document], existing: [names already there], applied?: name}

label: Default Swatches
params: {replace?: false} bring back the default swatches and colour groups of the document's colour mode that are missing (by name), as one undo step; replace: true makes the swatches exactly the defaults (art linked to a removed global swatch keeps its colour, unlinked) → {added: [names]}

label: Save Swatch Library…
params: {path?, format?: "vcswatches" (lossless JSON: colour models, global, spot, gradients, groups) | "gpl" (8-bit RGB palette; groups as `# Group:` comments) | "ase" (swatch exchange, binary: solid colors in their own model (RGB, CMYK, Lab, Gray) as global, spot or process colors, and color groups; gradients are left out, and a tint swatch is saved as the color it shows) | "css" (custom properties on :root) (default: the path's extension, else vcswatches), names?: [swatch or colour group names] (default: all; None and patterns are never saved), name?: library name (default: the document's), user?: false (save into the user library folder, listed under User Defined)} save the document's swatches as a library → {path, format, count: the swatches written (gpl and ase hold solid colors only, and css leaves freeform gradients out), library?: id when saved to the user folder}; without path or user → {data: the file's text, format, count}, or {dataBase64, format, count} for ase

label: Other Library…
params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, name?: file name (default: the path's)} load a .vcswatches, .gpl, .ase (swatch exchange) or .acb (color book, read only) library, or the swatches of any document VectorCraft opens (see document.formats), for the library panel (Window → Swatch Libraries lists it until the app quits; a file of the user library folder, or a file with the same extension and bytes as one there, opens as that User Defined library) → {library: id, name, count}

label: Copy to User Defined
params: {library: id or name of a loaded library (category "loaded", swatch.library.load)} copy it into the user library folder of the desktop app, whose libraries VectorCraft lists as User Defined every time it starts (a loaded library is listed until the app quits): a library file as it is, the swatches of a document or a library loaded from data as a .vcswatches file. A name the folder already has gets a number ("Brand 2.ase") and no file is replaced; when the folder already holds the same file, that file is used. The library is then listed as User Defined only, and until the app quits commands given its loaded id use the copy; a User Defined library comes back as it is → {library: its User Defined id, name, count, path, copied: false when nothing was written}

label: Add Freeform Point
params: {at: [x,y] (document coordinates), color? (default: the gradient's colour there), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), opacity?: 0..1 (or 0..100), spread?: 0..1 (or 0..100 %; the radius of pure colour around the point, a fraction of half the object's larger side; default 0), line?: true (join it to the selected point: extends the line ending there, else starts one), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} add a point to the freeform gradient (an unplaced one keeps its automatic points first) and select it → {index}

label: Edit Freeform Point
params: {index? (default: the selected point), at?: [x,y] (document coordinates), color?, keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), opacity?: 0..1 (or 0..100), spread?: 0..1 (or 0..100 %), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} move or recolour a point of the freeform gradient → {index}
