params: {layout?: "grid" (rows and columns) | "row" (one row) | "column" (one column), columns?: 1..10000 (grid; default ⌈√count⌉; never more than the count), gapX?: pt −1000000..1000000 (10), gapY?: pt −1000000..1000000 (gapX), centerOnArtboard?: false (true: the grid is centred on the artboard under the selection's centre, else the first; false: it starts at the selection's top-left)} lay the selected objects (the top-level ones) out in their stacking order from the back, left to right and top to bottom, as one undo step. Each cell is as wide as the widest object in its column and as tall as the tallest in its row, each object is centred in its cell, and everything is measured by visual bounds (strokes and effects as drawn) → {count}

label: Swap Objects
params: {size?: false (true: each also takes the other's width and height), scaleStrokes?: the Scale Strokes & Effects preference} swap the places (bounds centres) of the two selected objects, measured as object.setBounds measures them (Use Preview Bounds), as one undo step. Off unless exactly two objects are selected

label: Replace with Top Object
params: {fit?: "keep" (the copy keeps its size) | "bounds" (scaled to the replaced object's width and height) | "proportional" (scaled to fit inside them, in proportion) ("keep"), scaleStrokes?: the Scale Strokes & Effects preference, keep?: false (true: the replaced objects stay, under their copies)} put a copy of the topmost selected object centred on each of the other selected objects, in that object's place in the stacking order, as one undo step; sizes and centres are measured as object.setBounds measures them, and the copies are selected → {ids}

label: Set Size of Each
params: {width?: pt, height?: pt (at least one; each 0.001..1000000), proportional?: false (with only one of them given, the other follows in proportion; else it stays), reference?: 0..8 (the 9-point grid row by row from the top-left; 4, the centre: the point of each object that stays put), scaleStrokes?: the Scale Strokes & Effects preference} give each selected object (the top-level ones) that width and height, measured as object.setBounds measures them (Use Preview Bounds), as one undo step → {count}

label: Group Overlapping Objects
params: {} group the selected objects (the top-level ones, at most 20000) wherever their visual bounds overlap or touch, chains included (when A overlaps B and B overlaps C, all three go in one group), as one undo step. Only objects in the same layer or group are grouped together, objects that overlap nothing stay as they are, and each new group goes where its frontmost member was in the stacking order; the new groups and the objects left alone stay selected → {groups: [id…], grouped (how many objects went into groups)}

label: Randomize Opacity
params: {min?: % 0..100 (30), max?: % 0..100 (100; not less than min), seed?: whole number (0; the same seed, objects and range give the same opacities), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} give each selected object (the top-level ones) its own opacity, picked at random and evenly from min to max, as one undo step; it is the object's opacity, as the Transparency panel sets it → {count}

label: Sort Objects
params: {by?: "width" | "height" | "area" (width × height) | "x" (left edge) | "y" (top edge) | "opacity" (%) | "stacking" (stacking order, from the back) ("area"), apply?: one of the same ("stacking"), order?: "ascending" (small to large) | "descending" (large to small) | "random" ("ascending"), distribute?: false (true: the values step evenly from the smallest to the largest; false: the objects trade the values they have), seed?: whole number (0; the order "random" picks), scaleStrokes?: the Scale Strokes & Effects preference (width, height and area), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} sort the selected objects (the top-level ones, at most 20000) by the attribute `by` and give them the values of `apply` in that order, as one undo step: the first in order gets the smallest value. Sizes and places are measured and set as object.setBounds measures them (Use Preview Bounds), a width, height or area about each object's centre (an area in proportion); stacking order always trades places, and only among the objects in the same layer or group. A run that changes nothing makes no step → {count}

label: Simplify Anchors (Keep Shape)…
params: {tolerance?: 1..100 (20; higher removes more anchors and lets the outline move further from where it was, up to tolerance × 0.02 pt), protectCorners?: bool (false; anchors where the path turns by more than 30° stay), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} remove the anchors each path under the objects can do without, refitting the handles beside each so the outline keeps its shape, as one undo step; open ends stay → {ids, before, after} anchor counts

label: Health Check
params: {scope?: "selection"|"document" (default: the selection, or the document while nothing is selected), kinds?: [kind…] (default: all: emptyText, strayPoints (paths of one anchor), unpainted, zeroOpacity, duplicateObjects (a path stacked on an identical one, or type on the same type within 1 pt), offArtboard, duplicateAnchors (neighbours within 0.01 pt), tinyHandles (under 0.01 pt), collinearAnchors (corners on a straight run, turning less than sine 0.005), nearPoints (anchors within 0.01 pt of other paths' anchors), nearlyClosed (ends within 0.01 pt), filledOpenPaths (filled, unstroked open paths), needlessClipGroups (an unpainted clip that clips nothing, hides everything, or is a rectangle round all its art), needlessCompounds (one path or none), needlessGroups (one member or none, nothing of their own), emptyArtboards (the document only))} find issues without changing anything; locked and hidden objects are left out → {scope, total, findings: [{kind, label, count, ids (the objects, at most 1000), artboards (indexes)}]} for the kinds found

label: Show Issue
params: {kind: kind (see addon.cleanup.check), scope?: "selection"|"document"} select the objects with that issue → {kind, count, ids, artboards}

label: Fix All Issues
params: {scope?: "selection"|"document", kinds?: [kind…] (default: all; see addon.cleanup.check)} fix the issues addon.cleanup.check finds, in up to three rounds while a round still finds some (a fix can leave issues for another kind), as one undo step: what is empty, unpainted, invisible, duplicated or off the artboards goes, anchors merge, snap or go, tiny handles retract, paths close and needless groups, compound paths and clipping groups give way to their contents → {scope, total, fixed: {kind: count}}

label: Deep Ungroup…
params: {includeClipGroups?: bool (false: clipping groups, and the art inside them, stay as they are; true: they are ungrouped too and their clipping paths become plain paths), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} ungroup every level of the groups among the objects, as one undo step; each object keeps the opacity of the groups it was in → {ids (the objects left, selected), ungrouped (groups)}

label: Rejoin Path Pieces…
params: {gap?: pt 0..6 (0.1), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} weld the open paths under the objects whose ends lie within the gap of each other back into paths: an end joins one other end, the one the path turns least to go on into, pieces may run either way, and a chain whose ends meet closes; each path takes the place and paint of its topmost piece, as one undo step → {ids, joined (paths made), removed (pieces merged into them)}

label: Break Text
params: {by?: "lines"|"paragraphs"|"words"|"glyphs" (lines), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} each horizontal point or area type object becomes point type objects, one per line, paragraph, word or glyph, each where its characters were and with their character styles, as one undo step; spaces between pieces go, a paragraph's lines stay lines (a wrapped line ends in a line break), justified lines close up, and a paragraph broken out whole keeps its bullet (not its number; other pieces have no list markers). Type on a path, vertical type, threaded type and area type whose text doesn't fit stay as they are → {ids (the pieces, selected), skipped}

label: Combine Point Text
params: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} merge one-line horizontal point type into as few objects as it can, every glyph staying where it was: pieces turned and sheared alike whose baselines line up (within 0.4 em; the difference becomes baseline shift) join left to right, a space goes between pieces at least half a space apart, and tracking on the character before each piece keeps the spacing; each object keeps its character styles, and the leftmost piece of each run its place and paint, as one undo step → {ids (the objects made, selected), combined (pieces merged into them)}

label: Join Point Text
params: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} join one-line horizontal point type into one point type object, as one undo step: pieces turned and sheared like the top-left one are read as lines (baselines within 0.4 em of each other), top to bottom, each line's pieces left to right with a space between them; each line becomes a paragraph, left aligned, and keeps the distance between baselines as its leading. The text keeps its character styles; the object takes the top-left piece's place and paint, and the other pieces go → {id (selected), joined (pieces merged into it), lines}

label: Remove Breaks
params: {kind: "line"|"paragraph", ids?: [id…]} remove the forced line breaks (line) or paragraph returns (paragraph) in the characters selected with a Type tool, else in all the text of the selected type, as one undo step; a break between two words becomes a space → {ids, removed}

label: Split Text at Cursor
params: {} while a Type tool edits horizontal point or area type: the text before the selected characters, they and the text after become point type objects of their own (at a cursor: before and after it), each where its characters were, as one undo step; spaces at the ends of each piece go, and editing ends with the pieces selected → {ids}

label: Set Alignment, Keep Position
params: {align: "left"|"center"|"right", ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} align every paragraph of each horizontal point type object so, moving the object so its longest line stays where it is (one line: the text doesn't move), as one undo step → {ids (the objects changed)}

label: Reset Text Transform
params: {scale?: bool (false: the horizontal scale stays; true: it goes too, the object's and every character's), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} take the rotation, shear and reflection off each point type object, its size and the centre of its text staying, as one undo step → {ids (the objects changed)}

label: Replace Missing Fonts…
params: {font?: family (default: the default type font, Source Sans 3; any of its names)} set every character of the document's type whose font family isn't available in `font`, in the style it has closest to the one each had, as one undo step → {runs (style runs changed), font}

label: Select by Color Kind
params: {kind: "spotColors" (objects painted with a spot colour swatch, solid or in a gradient's stops) | "colorEffects" (objects carrying a visible colour adjustment effect, on themselves or on a fill or stroke) | "rgbImages" | "cmykImages" | "grayImages" (embedded or linked images whose pixels are RGB, CMYK, or grayscale or 1-bit)} select those objects among the ones Select All reaches, inside groups too; locked and hidden ones are left out → {count}

label: Apply as Filter
params: {effect: a colour adjustment's effect id (adjust.brightnessContrast, adjust.curves, adjust.hueSaturation, adjust.levels, adjust.shiftToColor, adjust.temperatureTint, addon.color.exposure, addon.color.desaturate, addon.color.duotone or addon.color.invert), params?: {…} (as effect.apply; missing keys take the dialog defaults), fill?: true, stroke?: true, includeImages?: true, includePatterns?: true, ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} recolour the objects and everything inside them as the live effect would draw them, but in their colours, as edit.colors.invert does (fills, strokes, type, gradient meshes, embedded images and pattern tiles), as one undo step; their effects stay. Duotone links a colour to its one tone's swatch as the live effect does → {changed}

label: Print Ink Fixes
params: {scope?: "selection" (the selection, or `ids`; by default, the document while nothing is selected) | "document" (every layer), inkLimit?: total ink % 1..400 (0 or left out: off), excludePureBlack?: true (black-only and grey colours keep their ink), removeWhiteOverprint?: false (white fills and strokes stop overprinting), overprintBlack?: black % 1..100 (black-only and grey fills and strokes this dark or darker overprint, as edit.colors.overprintBlack; 0 or left out: off), textOnly?: false (Overprint Black on type only), fill?: true, stroke?: true, ids?: [id…]} prepare a CMYK document's inks for print as one undo step: CMYK colours (solid, gradient stops, gradient meshes) with more total ink than inkLimit are scaled down to it (colours of spot swatches and Registration stay), white overprint is removed and black overprint set. Refused in RGB documents (File › Document Color Mode › CMYK Color first) → {changed, inkLimited: paints and meshes scaled, whiteOverprintRemoved: objects, blackOverprinted: objects}

label: Find Nearest Swatch
params: {library?: a swatch library's id or name (swatch.library.list: the built-in ones, and the colour books and libraries the user saved or loaded) or "document" (the document's swatches; the default), color?: colour (look this colour up; default: the selection's), fill?: true, stroke?: true (the selected objects' fills and strokes, their type's and those of the objects inside them: solid colours and gradient stops, once each, the first 100), count?: 1..50 (5), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} list the library's colour swatches closest to each colour, closest first, by CIEDE2000 difference (ΔE; under 1 hardly tells apart, about 2 to 3 close). Tint swatches, None and Registration aren't matched → {library, colors: [{values, hex, matches: [{name, values, hex, spot, deltaE}]}]}

label: Apply Nearest Swatch
params: {library?: as addon.color.nearestSwatch (default: "document"), fill?: true, stroke?: true, ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} give each solid colour and gradient stop of the selected objects' fills and strokes (their type's and those of the objects inside them; gradient meshes too) the colour of its nearest swatch in the library, as addon.color.nearestSwatch finds it, as one undo step: a global or spot swatch's colour links to it. A library's swatches the colours take are added to the document's first, as swatch.library.add adds them (a spot colour stays spot); images and patterns keep their colours → {changed: paints changed, swatches: [the document swatches the colours took], added: [swatches added to the document]}

label: Save a Timestamped Copy
params: {folder? (default: the document's own folder; needed for a document never saved), format?: vectorcraft|pdf|svg|svgz|ai|eps (default: the document's own, else vectorcraft), time?: Unix seconds (default: now)} write a copy of the document named <name>_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM.<ext> (the date and time in UTC; -2, -3… added when that name is taken) as File › Save a Copy writes it: the document keeps its path, title and modified state, and no undo step is made. Off where there is no clock (the web) → {path, format, bytes, warnings}

label: Export All Open Documents
params: {folder, format?: vectorcraft|pdf|svg|svgz|ai|eps (default: pdf)} write a copy of every open document, in tab order, to `folder` as File › Save a Copy writes it, each named after its document (<name>.<ext>; -2, -3… added when that name is taken, so no file is replaced), one self-contained file each with all of its art (images embedded or included, every artboard; no remembered save options apply): every document keeps its path, title and modified state, and no undo step is made. A document that can't be written is listed in `failed` and the others are still written; the active document stays active → {files: [{title, path, warnings}], failed: [{title, error}], format}

label: New Symbols from Layers
params: {layers?: [layer id…] (top-level layers; default: those highlighted in the Layers panel when two or more are, else every one), replace?: bool (false: the art stays; true: each layer's art is replaced by an instance of its symbol in the same place)} make one symbol of each layer's art as symbol.new makes one (registration in the centre), named after the layer (with a number added when a symbol has that name), as one undo step. Layers with no art are skipped, and with replace so are locked layers; with replace the instances are selected → {symbols: [name…], ids: [instance id…] (with replace), skipped: [{layer, name, reason: "empty"|"locked"}…]}

label: Anchor Eraser Brush
params: {points: [[x, y] | [x, y, pressure 0..1]…] (the brush's path, at most 100000 points), diameter?: pt 0.1..2500 (20; a point's pressure scales it), tolerance?: 1..100 (10; the outline may move up to tolerance × 0.02 pt), ignoreTolerance?: bool (false: every anchor under the brush that can go goes, its neighbours refitted), plain?: bool (false: true deletes them without refitting the handles beside them), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} remove the anchors of the paths under the objects that the brush passes over and that can go while the outline stays within the tolerance, as one undo step; open ends stay → {ids, removed}

label: Extend Path
params: {id, subpath?: index (0), end: "start"|"end", length?: pt (negative shortens; never all of it), to?: [x, y] (instead of length: the length that brings the end nearest this point), mode?: "straight"|"bezier" (stretch the last segment's curve, no anchor added)|"arc" (along the circle the end curves on, at most half way round) ("straight")} lengthen an open path at an end the way it runs there, or shorten it back along itself, as one undo step; with Keep Shared Points Together on, anchors coincident with an end that moves go with it → {id, length (pt)}

label: Measure & Inspect
params: {id, x, y, tolerance?: pt (3; how near an anchor counts as over it)} what the path reads at the point nearest (x, y): {subpath, closed, anchors, length, area (pt², an open subpath closed by a straight line), segment, t, point: [x, y], segmentLength, tangent (degrees counter-clockwise), radius (of curvature, null where straight), anchor?: {index, x, y, smooth, angle (at the anchor, null at an open end), in?: {length, angle}, out?: {length, angle}}}

label: Set Anchor
params: {x?, y?: pt (on the page), inLength?, outLength?: pt (0 retracts), inAngle?, outAngle?: degrees counter-clockwise} move the selected anchors (with their handles) and set their handles, as one undo step: direct-selected anchors, or every anchor of a path selected whole; a smooth anchor's other handle turns with the one set; with Keep Shared Points Together on, anchors coincident with one that moves go with it → {anchors}

label: Make Smooth
params: {ratio?: 0.1..0.5 (0.3905: a square's corners make a circle)} make the selected anchors smooth: a lone handle is mirrored; without handles, both stand at right angles to the bisector of the angle at the anchor, ratio × the nearer neighbour's distance long; two handles are put in line; an open end without handles aims at its neighbour's handle. One undo step → {anchors (changed)}

label: Make Corner
params: {retract?: bool (true: the handles go; false: they stay where they are and move apart)} make the selected anchors corners, as one undo step → {anchors (changed)}

label: Equalize Handles
params: {} give each selected anchor's two handles their average length (a missing one is made opposite the other), as one undo step → {anchors (changed)}

label: Remove Points, Keep Shape
params: {} remove the direct-selected anchors, refitting the handles beside each so the outline keeps its shape as best it can, as one undo step; open ends stay → {removed}

label: Add Points to Segments…
params: {count?: 1..100 (1)} add count anchors to each selected segment (a segment between two selected anchors, or every segment of a path selected whole), splitting it into pieces of equal length; the shape doesn't change. One undo step → {added}

label: Close Path
params: {mode?: "handles" (keep the ends' handles)|"straight" (a straight closing segment)|"smooth" (the ends made smooth), ratio?: 0.1..0.5 (0.3905, for smooth)} close the open subpaths of the selected paths, as one undo step → {closed}

label: Add Points at Crossings
params: {cut?: bool (false: add anchors where the paths cross; true: also cut them there), selfCrossings?: bool (false: where a path crosses itself too), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} where the paths under the objects cross one another, as one undo step; at most 10000 segments → {ids, crossings (anchors placed)}

label: Slide Anchor Along Path
params: {id, subpath?: index (0), anchor: index, t: -0.98..0.98 (where to: positive, a curve parameter on the segment after the anchor; negative, back from the end of the one before)} move an anchor along its path, the segments beside it refitted so the outline stays, as one undo step; ends of open paths don't slide; with Keep Shared Points Together on, anchors coincident with it go with it → {id, strayed (pt)}

label: Divide into Dashes
params: {dash?: pt 0.01..1000000 (10), gap?: pt 0..1000000 (0: the pieces touch), fit?: bool (false: exact lengths, the last piece of each run what is left; true: fit to corners and ends, every run between corners and ends holding whole dashes, all stretched or squeezed alike so it starts and ends on a dash), removeGaps?: bool (true: the gaps are left empty; false: they stay as pieces too)} cut the selected paths into separate open paths along the curve, each dash long with gap between them and keeping the path's appearance, as one undo step. Only the direct-selected segments (or those between two direct-selected anchors) are divided when there are any, the dash pattern running on across segments that follow one another; the rest of such a path stays, as pieces of its own. The pieces are selected; at most 100000 → {ids, dashes}

label: Expand Dashes into Paths
params: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} turn the dashed stroke of each path and compound path under the objects into separate open paths, one per dash, laid out as the stroke draws them (its dash pattern, offset and Align Dashes to Corners and Path Ends), each keeping the path's appearance with the dashes off, so the gaps are real gaps: a dash running all the way round a closed path stays closed, and with a round or projecting cap a dash of no length (a dot) becomes a path on its point. The top stroke's dashes are the ones expanded; its arrowheads go, and the path's fills stay on it, below its dashes. Paths without a dashed stroke stay as they are. One undo step; the dashes are selected; at most 100000 → {ids, dashes}

label: Parametric Shape
params: {center: [x, y], kind?: "rectangle"|"ellipse"|"polygon" (default)|"star"|"ring"|"arrow"|"cross"|"heart"|"gear"|"bubble" (a speech bubble), width?, height?: 0.01..16384 pt (100), rotation?: degrees clockwise (0: upright), count?: 3..1000 (a polygon's sides, a star's points, a gear's teeth), a?, b?: the kind's own values (star: inner radius 0.01..1 of the outer, 0.5; ring: hole 0.01..0.99 of the size, 0.5; arrow: head length and shaft width 0.05..0.95, 0.4 and 0.4; cross: bar offset −0.9..0.9 (0, − up) and arm thickness 0.05..0.95 (1/3); heart: notch depth and point roundness 0..1 (0.4 and 0); gear: tooth height 0.01..0.9 (0.2); bubble: tail height 0.05..0.9 (0.25) and tail tip −1..1 across (−0.4)), radius?: corner radius 0..16384 pt (0; no corner rounds past the middle of a side)} draw a parametric shape with the current paint, selected, as one undo step; it stays editable with addon.pathtools.shape.set until its anchors are edited (moving, turning or scaling it keeps it) → {id, shape}

label: Edit Parametric Shape
params: {id, kind?, center?, width?, height?, rotation?, count?, a?, b?, radius?} change a parametric shape's numbers (as addon.pathtools.shape.create takes them; a new kind takes its own defaults for the values not given), as one undo step; with none, or the same ones, nothing changes → {id, shape (its numbers now)}

label: Convert to Parametric Shape
params: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} make each plain closed path that is a rectangle, an ellipse or a polygon with equal sides and corners (stretched along its own axes at most) a parametric shape of the same outline, as one undo step → {ids (converted)}

label: Set Corners
params: {ids?: [id…] (the selection), anchors?: [index…] (of each path's outline with no corners cut; else its direct-selected anchors, or all of them), items?: [{id, anchors?}…] (instead of ids: each path with its own anchors), radius: pt 0..1000000 (drawn no larger than fits), kind?: "round"|"invertedRound"|"chamfer" (each corner's own)} cut live corners at the anchors that can have one, as one undo step → {ids, corners (how many)}

label: Remove Corners
params: {ids?: [id…] (the selection), anchors?: [index…] (of each path's outline with no corners cut; else its direct-selected anchors, or all of them), items?: [{id, anchors?}…] (instead of ids: each path with its own anchors)} make those live corners sharp again, as one undo step → {ids, corners (how many)}

label: Merge Shared Edge
params: {a, b: two path ids (they needn't be selected), at: [x, y] (where), diameter?: pt 0.25..200 (20; how near `at` the edge is looked for), tolerance?: pt 0..3 (0.002; how near two anchors count as coincident), follow?: "average" (half way between the two)|"a"|"b" (keep that path's outline), ends?: bool (false: true makes an end even where the paths could merge)} where the paths touch at two coincident anchors, one each side of `at`, replace the stretches between them with one shared edge; stretches much longer one than the other (by over 10%) or leaving an end at over 120° aren't merged. Otherwise make an end there: two near anchors meet, and an anchor only one path has there is matched by a new one on the other. Each path stays closed or open; one undo step → {a, b, made: "edge"|"end"|"nothing" (merged already)}

label: Keep Shared Points Together
params: {enabled?: bool (default: the opposite of now)} Keep Shared Points Together: whether anchors coincident (within the Shared Edge Merge Tool's `tolerance`) with one that Slide Anchor Along Path, Extend Path or Set Anchor moves move with it, on any editable path (the `together` option of tool `sharedEdge`, kept with the preferences; off by default) → {enabled}

label: Smart Pen
params: {id, subpath?: index (default: the last open subpath), x, y, in?: [x, y], out?: [x, y], segment?: "straight" (the segment into the new anchor is a line: the previous anchor's handle on it goes, and the new anchor's incoming one)|"curved" (the previous anchor gets a handle on it if it has none: in line with its other handle, or with a straight segment before it)} add an anchor at the end of an open subpath of path id (default: the handles as given, the previous anchor as it is), as one undo step; the new anchor is selected → {anchor}

label: Close Path
params: {id, subpath?: index (default: the last open subpath), segment?: "straight"|"curved" (default: the closing segment takes the handles its ends have)} close an open subpath of two anchors or more, as one undo step

label: Straight or Curved Segment
params: {id, subpath?: index (0), segment: index, curved: bool} make a segment straight (its handles retracted) or curved (each end without a handle on it gets one, in line with its other handle or with a straight segment before it), as one undo step → {changed}

label: Remove Points, Keep Shape
params: {id, subpath?: index (0), anchor: index, plain?: bool (false: the handles beside it are refitted so the outline keeps its shape, and an open end takes its segment with it; true: it goes and the handles beside it stay as they are)} remove one anchor, as one undo step; a subpath keeps two anchors (three when closed)

label: Convert Anchor Point
params: {id, subpath?: index (0), anchor: index, ratio?: 0.1..0.5 (0.3905)} a smooth anchor becomes a corner with its handles where they are; any other anchor is made smooth by the auto-smooth rule (a lone handle mirrored; without handles both at right angles to the bisector of the angle at it, ratio × the nearer neighbour's distance long). One undo step → {smooth}

label: Reshape Segment
params: {id, subpath?: index (0), segment: index, t?: 0..1 (where it was grabbed, 0.5; held to 0.05..0.95), dx, dy: pt, mode?: "free" (both handles move, the one nearer the grab more)|"keepAngles" (each handle keeps its direction)|"symmetric" (both handles at right angles to the chord, at one length) ("free")} bend a segment so the point grabbed moves by (dx, dy); missing handles grow out of their anchors and a smooth anchor stays smooth. One undo step

label: Next Segment
params: {curved: bool} whether a click with the Smart Pen Tool adds a curved segment or a straight one (the tool's `next` option, kept with the preferences) → {next: "straight"|"curved"}

label: Close or Join
params: {} with exactly two open path ends direct-selected, join them as path.join does; else close the selected open paths keeping their ends' handles, as addon.pathtools.close does. One undo step

label: Open…
params: {path} open any readable file (see document.formats) as a new document; templates open untitled

label: Save
params: {…as document.save} = document.save {path?, format?, options?, svg?: {…SVG options}}: .vectorcraft, .ai (a PDF that reopens editable), .pdf, .svg or .svgz (default: the document's own path and format)

label: Export…
params: {…as document.export} = document.export {path?, format?, artboard?, range?, scale?, …} (no path → dataBase64)

label: Export for Screens…
params: {folder?, zip?, artboards? | range? | fullDocument? | assets?, includeBleed?, includeArtboardFill?, subfolders?, preset?, formats?, settings?, prefix?} = document.exportForScreens (no folder → the files, or one zip, as dataBase64)

label: Select Tool
params: {tool} e.g. selection, directSelection, pen, rectangle, ellipse, polygon, star, lineSegment

label: Tool Option
params: {key?, value? | values?: {key: value…}, tool?: id (default: the active tool)} → the tool's options (`{}` reads them); kept options last across tool switches
